meta.source: Energy Trust of Oregon, Water Heater Serial Number Decoder (2025); Bradford White, Determine the Age of My Water Heater; Rheem/Ruud official age lookup; U.S. CPSC recall notices (Navien)
meta.notes: Only brands whose format we could confirm in an opened source are listed. Patterns are tried in order. Two-digit years take the latest matching year that is not in the future. Letter-year codes repeat every 20 years, so the decoder returns the latest year and lists the earlier ones; the unit's look and the dates on its labels settle which is right. Rinnai, Noritz, Takagi and Bosch are not decoded: no manufacturer or government source for their date code could be opened (third-party guides disagree with each other), so the calculator asks for the manufacture year. Rheem and Ruud also offer their own lookup, which beats any decoder.

bradford-white.label: Bradford White
bradford-white.source: Bradford White: first two characters of the serial are the year and month (year letters exclude I, O, Q, R, U, V; month letters A to M exclude I); Energy Trust of Oregon gives the earlier cycles (A = 1964, 1984, 2004)

patterns.example: DF******* → June 1967, 1987, 2007 or 2027 (latest not in the future)

rheem.label: Rheem / Ruud
rheem.source: Rheem/Ruud official age lookup (tested 2026-11-13: serials that start with a plant letter, then a two-digit week and a two-digit year, return that week's date); Energy Trust of Oregon for older all-digit serials (two-digit month, then two-digit year, example 0794****** = July 1994)

patterns.source: Energy Trust of Oregon decoder: 0794****** or 0794F***** = July 1994

ao-smith.label: A. O. Smith
ao-smith.source: Energy Trust of Oregon: since 2008, an 11-character serial whose first two positions are the year followed by a two-digit week (example 0805A…); before 2008 the second letter is the month (A to N, no I) followed by a two-digit year (example *H06… = August 2006)

state.label: State
state.source: Energy Trust of Oregon: since 2008 State uses the A. O. Smith code (two-digit year, two-digit week); before 2008 a one-letter month (A to N, no I) followed by a two-digit year (example C05… = March 2005)

patterns.example: 0904******* → 2009, week 4 (Energy Trust labels this example April 2009, which does not match its own year-week rule; we follow the rule)

american.label: American
american.source: Energy Trust of Oregon: American uses a two-digit year followed by a two-digit week (example 9746****** = week 46 of 1997); American has been part of A. O. Smith since 2001 and makes the Whirlpool brand

navien.label: Navien
navien.source: U.S. CPSC recall notices for Navien tankless water heaters (2018, 2019): after the four-digit model code and one more character, the next two digits are the year, the next character is the month (X = October) and the next two digits are the day; example 18709 = July 9, 2018. Navien: the serial is on the outside right of the unit, between two barcodes, 15 to 16 characters long.

patterns.notes: CPSC confirms 1 to 9 for January to September and X for October. Y and Z for November and December follow the same sequence; no opened source shows them, so treat those two months as likely, not confirmed.

brandOptions.source: Dropdown for the age calculator. decodeAs = which brand's date code applies; empty = not decodable, ask for the year. Aliases come from the Energy Trust of Oregon decoder (Whirlpool is made by American; State/Kenmore; General Electric under Rheem).

options.label: Whirlpool
options.caveat: Whirlpool water heaters are made by American (part of A. O. Smith), so the American code is used.

options.label: GE
options.caveat: Older GE water heaters were made by Rheem, so the Rheem code is used. Newer GE units may use another maker's code; if the date looks wrong, enter the year from the label.

options.label: Kenmore
options.caveat: Kenmore units were made by more than one manufacturer. The State code is used, which fits State-made Kenmore units only; check the year against the label.
